# Busabase

An open-source database and workspace for AI agents.

Visit BusabaseFree4.3

Built with love by Shushant Lakhyani. Building bestproductivityresources.com

## What is Busabase?

Busabase gives AI agents structured data, durable knowledge, reusable skills and runnable apps in one local-first, self-hostable workspace, with human review on the writes that matter.

## Pros

 Local-first and self-hostable
 Human review on important writes
 MIT licensed

## Cons

 Aimed at developers building agent workflows
 Setup takes technical know-how

## Who should use Busabase

Developers who need a durable, reviewable data layer for AI agents.

## Who may not need it

People who only use chat assistants.

## Busabase alternatives

# Compare Busabase

Honest comparisons against the products people actually evaluate Busabase alongside. Each page states where the alternative is the better choice, because a comparison you can tell is rigged is worth nothing to the person reading it.

Connect your agentWhat makes a system of record

## Comparisons

Busabase vs ChatGPT Space

ChatGPT Space, launched 29 September 2026, gives a team, ChatGPT, Codex and Dots one home for pages, files and Sites, co-edited in real time. It reviews AI text in place. The open question is the data other agents read as fact: where it lives, and who decides a changed value becomes true.

Choose ChatGPT Space when the work is documents your team writes with AI inside ChatGPT.

Busabase vs Notion [...] The concession section is real.

Every page has a "where the alternative is better" section written well enough that the other team would agree with it.

Organized by the job you are doing

, not by a checkmark table engineered to favor us.

Cooperative where that is the truth.

Several of these products sit at a different layer than Busabase, and the honest recommendation is to use both.

## Related

What makes a store a system of record for AI agents — the underlying argument most of these comparisons rest on.

Connect your agent — if you would rather test the difference than read about it. [...] Busabase vs Notion

Notion 3.6 lets Claude and Cursor work in your workspace and records what they changed. The question is no longer who is allowed in — it is who holds the write path. Notion's answer is an Enterprise audit log, which tells you what changed after it changed.

Choose Notion when the document is the deliverable and your team already lives there.

Busabase vs Supabase

Supabase tells you not to connect agents to your production database. That is correct advice, and it leaves one question open: where does the agent's work go instead? A comparison about which layer your problem lives on.

Choose Supabase when you are building an application — it is not competing for this job.
